Sable Harrow.narrative: I keep the lamp-oil stall at the night market, and I have kept it alone since the Surge took my husband and the lower quay both. Oil, wicks, salt: nothing anyone can do without, and nothing I give away. The quay's stone price is robbery and the Warden knows it, but I pay my stall fee and I keep my own counsel. I trust the tide and my own count, and not much else.
values: keeping the stall and the marks it makes
independence: owe no one more than you must
the night market and the crews who trade there
her son's future on the quay
goals: keep the stall solvent through the winter
clear the debt to Bramwell Tallow for the tar
keep Tam out of the water and out of trouble
find cheap stone where the Warden does not look
Sable Harrow.mood: wary, brisk, tired behind the eyes

relations.name: Tam Harrow
relations.label: son
relations.note: He carries my loads and asks no questions, which is worth more than marks.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I owe him for a barrel of tar and he reminds me of it every market.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: trade neighbour
relations.note: She knows the price of everything, and so do I; we get on well enough.

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: customer
relations.note: She buys my oil for the night crews and pays on time, mostly.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She speaks for the quay and collects my stall fee; I keep my head down when she walks the stalls.

relations.name: Sella Tallow
relations.label: friend of my son
relations.note: A good girl for Tam to run with; she minds her mother's stall better than most.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She set my wrist after the Surge and asked nothing for it, which I have not forgotten.

relations.name: Tam Sedge
relations.label: carrier
relations.note: He shifted a load for me and never once asked what was under the sacking; that's worth a few marks in his mother's smoke shed, and worth keeping quiet about.

memories.gist: The night the surge came I was on the stall and the water took the lower quay and my husband with it.
I opened the stall the next week because the crews still needed oil and I still needed marks.
Tam carried his first load for Bramwell Tallow last spring and came home proud with a mark in his fist.
A Sootwood woodcutter offered me stone cheap off the back of a cart, and I did not ask where it came from.
I sold that stone on the quay as salvage before the Warden's man came round the stalls.

stances.why: Everyone on the quay says they will pay; half of them do.
Kettlebridge sells us our own wall at a price that keeps the lower quay drowned.
It is the only thing between me and the poor terrace.
The quay is built on salvage; mine is no worse than anyone's.
The sea took his father and I will not give it the son as well.

Sable Harrow.secret: She buys stone from a Sootwood woodcutter who lifts it off the Kettlebridge road and sells it on the quay as salvage; she fears the Warden finding out more than she fears the woodcutter.

Tam Harrow.narrative: I carry loads for the stalls and for Bramwell Tallow, and I listen to the night crews talk about the harbour mouth and the stone price. My father drowned in the Surge before I was old enough to crew with him, so I am the man of the stall now. Sella Tallow is the only one who talks to me like I am not a child. I want a boat of my own one day, or at least a share in a catch.
values: the night crews and their talk
getting a place on a boat
goals: earn enough carrying to buy a good knife
learn the harbour mouth from the crews
keep his mother from worrying about the Warden

relations.name: Sable Harrow
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She works the stall all night and I carry for her; I do not ask her where the cheap loads come from.

relations.name: Sella Tallow
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She minds her mother's stall and knows every price on the quay; she talks to me proper.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: employer
relations.note: He pays me a mark a load and shouts if I am slow.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: stallkeeper
relations.note: She slips me a pie end when I have carried for her, and asks after my mother.

relations.name: Wick Cormorant
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He fishes with his father and says he will take me out when I am bigger.

memories.gist: The surge came at night and I woke in the loft with water in the street; my father did not come back.
I carried my first load for Bramwell Tallow and he paid me a whole mark.
I helped my mother shift a cart of stone to the stall and she told me not to say where it came from.
Sella Tallow taught me to count the night crews' bowls so her mother does not lose marks.

stances.why: My mother says the crews talk too much and the Warden listens.
Every man on the quay who has a boat has a house; every man without one is one storm from nothing.
My mother says it, and the crews say it, and the lower quay is still broken.
